question: {"question": "What are the values and meaning of TIMEOUT_CYCLES and BUILD_STAMP?", "proposed_default": "TIMEOUT_CYCLES 100000 is only the shell host-side wait with no effect on the block; BUILD_STAMP is passed through unused"}

reply.answer: TIMEOUT_CYCLES is 100000 according to the parameters section. The specification gives no meaning for it, so the proposed default that it is a shell host-side wait is not supported. BUILD_STAMP does not appear in the specification, so its value and meaning are not specified.

question: {"question": "What happens to ticks written while earlier ticks are still pending?", "proposed_default": "A write replaces the pending count with n"}

{"question": "Does every accepted command with status 0 count as carried out, including telemetry start, stop when already off, and status?", "proposed_default": "Yes, every status 0 reply counts as one command carried out"}
{"question": "Is the telemetry period a 16-bit value, high byte first?", "proposed_default": "Yes, 16-bit big-endian"}
{"question": "When is the busy bit of the status word 1?", "proposed_default": "From the first byte of a packet until its reply or drop is complete"}

{"question": "Which counter does each refusal use?", "proposed_default": "Status 1, 2, 3, 5 count in the type/length/register/access counter; status 4 counts in repeated (difference 0) or out-of-order (difference 32768 to 65535)"}
{"question": "Is the status reply payload length 17?", "proposed_default": "Yes, 7*2 + 2 + 1 = 17 bytes, length byte 17"}

reply.answer: Yes. The STATUS payload is seven 16-bit counters (14 bytes), a 16-bit telemetry frame count (2 bytes), and a TLM_ON byte (1 byte), which totals 17 bytes. The spec does not state the length byte explicitly, so this follows from the listed contents.
reply.quote: 'STATUS: seven 16-bit counters, telemetry frame count (16 bit), TLM_ON byte, all before this command is counted.'
